prompt_protocol.initial_template: Author a Bit Code plan for task {task}. Task: {intent}. Use plan_version {version}. Context: {context}. Permitted edit schema: {schema}. base_commit is {base_commit}. Return JSON only.
prompt_protocol.repair_suffix: Previous output failed: {diagnostic}. Return only the corrected plan object.
prompt_protocol.envelope_shape: structurally enforced; repair loop evaluates content errors only
prompt_protocol.graph_context: node path, language, and bounded current Node.source only

task_intents.rust-replace: Change Trace::final_env to use map_or_else(Env::new, |step| step.env.clone()).
task_intents.rust-insert: Insert a module-level pub fn trace_fixture_marker() -> usize that returns 1.
task_intents.python-replace: Change greet so it returns hello(name).upper().
task_intents.python-insert: Insert a module-level sample_fixture_marker function that returns 1.

semantic_verification.declared_checks: required task-specific semantic check and must pass

rationale.on_failure: The v2 run's authoring_plan_json_schema inferred {"type": "string"} for on_failure, so the model could emit any string; 4 of 7 completed v2 responses failed on a wrong on_failure value. schema_version 3 requires on_failure to be grammar-constrained to the exact enum mirrored from OnFailure in crates/aether-app/src/project/planfile/schema.rs (rollback_plan, rollback_step, stop), so the repair loop is left to handle genuine content errors rather than an unconstrained free-form string.
rationale.success_criterion: The v2 criterion required 4 common successes across both arms, but the text arm's complete-file prompts timed out on a 1.5B model in a 2.3 GB VM for 13 of 20 v2 attempts, including three unrecoverable Rust text arms. That made the common-successes threshold unmeetable for infrastructure reasons unrelated to authoring quality, so it measured nothing. schema_version 3 makes the primary criterion graph-arm semantic successes only, threshold 4 of 8. The text arm keeps running and its results keep being recorded, but they are reported as secondary and bounded by this documented hardware ceiling, not used to gate pass/fail.
